title: German government plans partnership with Nvidia on AI, Handelsblatt reports
source_used: Reuters text via Euronext; details from BigGo Finance and Investing.com (via Yahoo Finance Australia)
key_facts: Germany plans a wide-ranging AI cooperation agreement with Nvidia to boost AI take-up in German industry, per business daily Handelsblatt citing people familiar with the matter (15 Oct 2026).
It would be announced next week at the Invest in Germany conference in Berlin, where Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is a guest.
Two aims: a basis for physical AI tools used to train robots or self-driving vehicles, and high-performance AI models for industry.
The agreement would involve investments in the hundreds of millions of euros.
It would be built around SOOFI (Sovereign Open Source Foundation Models), launched in Germany last year with research institutions, universities and AI companies.
The German government had no immediate comment; last month it said it remained committed to AI capacity and Europe's digital sovereignty.
BigGo and Investing.com add: Chancellor Friedrich Merz and Huang are expected to unveil it Monday, funding may rent computing from Deutsche Telekom, about twelve German firms may join.
quote_evidence: Germany plans a wide-ranging cooperation agreement with US chip maker Nvidia to boost the take-up of artificial intelligence in German industry, business daily Handelsblatt said on Thursday, citing people familiar with the issue.
The newspaper said the agreement would involve investments in the hundreds of millions of euros.
why_it_matters_hint: Germany may tie its industrial AI push to a US chip supplier while stressing digital sovereignty.
notes: TradingView link returned no text; Reuters text read on Euronext. Plan from unnamed sources, not signed or confirmed.
